L000030	\begin{abstract}
L000031	Despite major experimental progresses in time-resolved
L000032	and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, a  quantitative,
L000033	microscopic framework for interpreting
L000034	exciton-induced modifications of electronic band structures --
L000035	applicable even beyond the low-density limit -- is still lacking.
L000036	Here we close this gap by introducing a unified
L000037	approach that links the dynamics of
L000038	coherent and incoherent excitons to distinct and experimentally observable
L000039	excitonic sidebands.
L000040	Our central result is a general, first-principles
L000041	formula for time-resolved photoemission spectra, applicable across a
L000042	broad range of temperatures, excitation densities, and pump–probe
L000043	delays. This advance provides a predictive tool for
L000044	quantitatively tracking excitonic dynamics in complex
L000045	materials.
L000046	\end{abstract}
L000047	
L000048	\maketitle
L000049	
L000050	
L000051	
L000052	
L000053	{\em Introduction.--}
L000054	The concept of excitons as quasiparticles in semiconductors and
L000055	insulators has long been central to the interpretation of optical
L000056	spectra, where it underpins the understanding of subgap resonances
L000057	and above-gap structures in absorbance and reflectance
L000058	measurements~\cite{onida_electronic_2002}. Optical probes, however,
L000059	are fundamentally restricted to bright, zero–center-of-mass-momentum
L000060	excitons and primarily access their energies. By contrast,
L000061	angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) reveals
L000062	a far
L000063	richer and more detailed
L000064	picture~\cite{zhang_angle-resolved_2022,boschini_time-resolved_2024,xu_time-domain_2025}.
L000065	In particular, time-resolved ARPES (TR-ARPES)
L000066	has recently
L000067	emerged as a powerful platform for exciton physics, enabling  direct access
L000068	to bright, momentum-dark, and spin-dark
L000069	excitons~\cite{madeo_directly_2020,dendzik_observation_2020,tanimura_time_2020,wallauer_momentum-resolved_2021,fukutani_detecting_2021,kunin_momentum-resolved_2023,bange_probing_2024,gosetti_unveiling_2024}.
L000070	Beyond exciton energies, TR-ARPES uniquely resolves excitonic
L000071	wavefunctions in both band and momentum
L000072	space~\cite{man_experimental_2021,dong_direct_2021,meneghini_hybrid_2023,mori_spin-polarized_2023}.
L000073	
L000074	Although TR-ARPES~\cite{na_advancing_2023} has led to
L000075	informative experimental spectra,  a rigourous
L000076	connection with the underlying exciton dynamics  is still
L000077	lacking.
L000078	After pumping below the bandgap,
L000079	the nonequilibrium exciton
L000080	fluid~\cite{haug2009quantum,lindberg_effective_1988,ostreich_non-stationary_1993,hannewald_excitonic_2000,koch_semiconductor_2006}
L000081	drives the motion of the nuclear
L000082	lattice.
L000083	The scattering between electrons and phonons
L000084	destroys exciton
L000085	coherence~\cite{madrid_phonon-induced_2009,nie_ultrafast_2014,dey_optical_2016,sangalli_an-ab-initio_2018,stefanucci_from-carriers_2021,perfetto_real-time_2023}
L000086	and diffuses
L000087	excitons~\cite{bertoni_generation_2016,uddin_neutral_2020,perfetto_ultrafast_2021,stefanucci_excitonic_2025}.
L000088	Bright coherent excitons are converted
L000089	-- typically in less than a few hundreds of femtoseconds~\cite{moody_intrinsic_2015,selig_exciton_2016,jakubczyk_impact_2018} -- into
L000090	bright and dark incoherent excitons.
L000091	TR-ARPES spectra of {\em coherent} excitons have been successfully
L000092	described~\cite{perfetto_pump-driven_2019,perfetto_time-resolved_2020,perfetto_floquet_2020,chan_giant_2023,pareek_driving_2026}.
L000093	However,  a first principles many-body framework for
L000094	the {\em incoherent} regime -- applicable even beyond the
L000095	domain of low excitation densities -- remains underdeveloped~\cite{perfetto_first-principles_2016,steinhoff_exciton_2017,rustagi_photoemission_2018,christiansen_theory_2019}.
L000096	In this Letter, we identify distinct signatures of coherent and
L000097	incoherent excitons in the TR-ARPES signal and provide a unified
L000098	theory of excitonic sidebands emerging from different exciton states.
L000099	The main finding is a
L000100	ready-to-use first-principles formula for interpreting TR-ARPES spectra
L000101	across a wide range
L000102	of temperatures, excitation densities and pump-probe delays.
L000103	
L000104	{\em Photocurrent.--}
L000105	The rate of photoelectrons with energy $\e$ and parallel
L000106	momentum $\blk$, ejected by a high-energy probe
L000107	pulse $a(t)=ae^{-i\w_{0}t}+{\rm h.c.}$
L000108	impinging on the crystal after a delay $\t$ from the pump, is
L000109	proportional to~\cite{freericks_theoretical_2009,perfetto_first-principles_2016}
L000110	\begin{align}
L000111	I_{\blk}(\t,\e)&\propto-i|a|^{2}\sum_{\m\m'}
L000112	D_{\m\blk}(\e)D^{\ast}_{\m'\blk}(\e)
L000113	G^{<}_{\m\m'\blk}(\t,\w_{0}-\e),
L000114	\label{tdph2}
L000115	\end{align}
L000116	where  $D_{\m\blk}(\e)$ is the
L000117	photoemission matrix element for an electron
L000118	with band-momentum index $(\m\blk)$.
L000119	Henceforth, we use $\m=c$ for conduction bands and $\m=v$ for valence
L000120	bands. The nonequilibrium electronic
L000121	properties of the crystal are encoded in the Fourier transform,
L000122	$G^{<}(\t,\w)$,
L000123	of the lesser Green's function $G^{<}(t,t')$ with respect to the
L000124	time-difference $t-t'$ for a given center-of-mass-time (delay) $\t=(t+t')/2$.
L000125	In the quasiparticle approximation
L000126	$G^{<}_{\m\m'\blk}(\t,\w)=\d_{\m\m'}2\p i
L000127	f_{\m\blk}(\t)\d(\w-\e_{\m\blk}(\t))$, and the spectrum is peaked at
L000128	the quasiparticle energies $\e_{\m\blk}(\t)$ -- with an intensity
L000129	proportional to the
L000130	nonequilibrium populations $f_{\m\blk}(\t)$.
L000131	Since our primary interest is in the excitonic sidebands appearing
L000132	above the valence band maximum,
L000133	we  focus exclusively on the contribution of conduction electrons  to
L000134	the photoemission signal. Consequently, we restrict
L000135	the sum over $\m,\m'$ in Eq.~(\ref{tdph2}) to the conduction bands.
L000136	
L000137	{\em TR-ARPES formula.--}
L000138	The interacting
L000139	nonequilibrium $G^{<}$ for conduction electrons can be calculated
L000140	from~\cite{svl-book_2025}
L000141	\begin{align}
L000142	G^{<}_{\blk}(\t,\w)=G^{R}_{\blk}(\t,\w)\S^{<}_{\blk}(\t,\w)G^{A}_{\blk}(\t,\w),
L000143	\label{G<}
L000144	\end{align}
L000145	where all quantities are matrices with conduction band indices.
L000146	We remark that this way of calculating $G^{<}$
L000147	differs from
L000148	earlier
L000149	attempts~\cite{perfetto_first-principles_2016,steinhoff_exciton_2017}, which
L000150	rely on the fluctuation-dissipation {\em ansatz}
L000151	$G^{<}_{\blk}(\t,\w)=i f(\w-\m_{c})A_{\blk}(\t,\w)$, where $f$ is the Fermi
L000152	function with a conduction-band
L000153	chemical potential $\m_{c}$ fixed by the excitation density,
L000154	and $A_{\blk}(\t,\w)$ is the nonequilibrium spectral function. This
L000155	ansatz is problematic for frequencies $\w$ below the gap since, at finite
L000156	temperature and/or out of
L000157	equilibrium, the addition and removal energies
L000158	overlap.
L000159	The retarded and advanced Green's functions
L000160	\begin{align}
L000161	G^{R}_{\blk}(\t,\w)=[G^{A}_{\blk}(\t,\w)]^{\dag}=[\w-\callE_{\blk}(\t)-\S^{R}_{\blk}(\t,\w)],
L000162	\end{align}
L000163	with $[\callE_{\blk}(\t)]_{\m\m'}\equiv \d_{\m\m'}\e_{\m\blk}(\t)$,
L000164	and the lesser
L000165	Green's function in Eq.~(\ref{G<}) can be calculated once an approximation for the
L000166	electronic self-energy $\S$ is available.
L000167	
L000168	
L000169	Let us consider  pump fields with frequencies
L000170	below the bandgap, ensuring that only discrete states are
L000171	explored during the time evolution.
L000172	We demonstrate below that Hartree plus statically
L000173	screened exchange (HSEX) effectively capture
L000174	the coherent regime, while T-matrix plus exchange
L000175	accurately describes the incoherent regime.
L000176	Remarkably, the full self-energy can be compactly
L000177	expressed as
L000178	\begin{subequations}
L000179	\begin{align}
L000180	\S^{R}_{cc'\blk}(\t,\w)&=\sum_{\l\blQ v}\s^{\l\blQ
L000181	v}_{cc'\blk}(\t,\w)\;,
L000182	\label{sigmaR}
L000183	\\
L000184	\S^{<}_{cc'\blk}(\t,\w)&=\sum_{\l\blQ v}
L000185	f(\w-E_{\l\blQ}(\t)-\e_{v\blk-\blQ}(\t))
L000186	\nn\\
L000187	&\times[\s^{\l\blQ v}_{cc'\blk}(\t,\w)-\s^{\l\blQ
L000188	v\ast}_{cc'\blk}(\t,\w)]\;,
L000189	\label{sigma<}
L000190	\end{align}
L000191	\label{sigma}
L000192	\end{subequations}
L000193	where the sum runs over all valence bands and over all exciton states $\l$ of
L000194	momentum $\blQ$. In the Fermi function of Eq.~(\ref{sigma<}),
L000195	the quasiparticle energies
L000196	$\e_{\m\blk}(\t)$ and exciton energies $E_{\l\blQ}(\t)$ are those of
L000197	the {\em nonequilibrium} system.
L000198	The key quantity in Eq.~(\ref{sigma}) is the function
L000199	\begin{align}
L000200	\s^{\l\blQ v}_{cc'\blk}(\t,\w)=K^{\l\blQ}_{cv\blk}\;
L000201	\frac{N_{\l\blQ}(\t)}{\w-E_{\l\blQ}(\t)-\e_{v\blk-\blQ}(\t)+i\eta}\;
L000202	K^{\l\blQ\ast}_{c'v\blk}-i\eta\;,
L000203	\label{sigmasmall}
L000204	\end{align}
L000205	where $\eta$ is a positive infinitesimal, and the amplitude
L000206	\begin{align}
L000207	K^{\l\blQ}_{cv\blk}=(\e^{\rm eq}_{c\blk}-\e^{\rm eq}_{v\blk-\blQ}-E^{\rm eq}_{\l\blQ})A^{\l
L000208	\blQ}_{cv\blk-\blQ}
L000209	\label{contrdef}
L000210	\end{align}
L000211	is expressed in terms of the
L000212	equilibrium band structure $\e^{\rm eq}_{\m\blk}$,
L000213	exciton energies $E^{\rm eq}_{\l\blQ}$ and wavefunctions $A^{\l
L000214	\blQ}_{cv\blk}$. Notably, the full self-energy
L000215	depends only on the {\em total} number of
L000216	excitons at the probing time $\t$~\cite{stefanucci_excitonic_2025}
L000217	\begin{align}
L000218	N_{\l\blQ}(\t)=\d_{\blQ,\bz}|\r_{\l}(\t)|^{2}+
L000219	N^{\rm inc}_{\l\blQ}(\t),
L000220	\label{N=c+ixb}
L000221	\end{align}
L000222	with $|\r_{\l}|^{2}$ the number of coherent excitons,
L000223	and $N^{\rm inc}_{\l\blQ}$ the number of incoherent
L000224	excitons.
L000225	In Appendix~\ref{findensapp} we present a
L000226	practical method to extract the nonequilibrium energies
L000227	$\e_{\m\blk}(\t)$ and $E_{\l\blQ}(\t)$
L000228	directly from $N_{\l\blQ}(\t)$.
L000229	Equations~(\ref{G<}-\ref{sigmasmall}) are the main
L000230	result of this Letter. They
L000231	 provide a first-principles formula
L000232	to calculate TR-ARPES spectra for any pump-probe delay, and for a
L000233	wide range of temperatures and excitation densities.
L000234	The only input quantities are
L000235	the exciton
L000236	populations $N_{\l\blQ}(\t)$, which
L000237	can be determined by, e.g., solving the excitonic Bloch
L000238	equations~\cite{thranhardt_quantum_2000,selig_exciton_2016,brem_exciton_2018,stefanucci_excitonic_2025}.
L000239	
L000240	
L000241	{\em Coherent regime.--} Here we briefly revisit the
L000242	theory of the coherent regime, and offer an alternative perspective.
L000243	Without any
L000244	loss of generality we set
L000245	the time origin, $t=0$, after the action of the pump pulse. For weak
L000246	pumping the excitation density is low, and
L000247	the state of the system at positive times is given by the quantum
L000248	superposition
L000249	$|\Q(t)\ket=|\Q_{g}\ket+\sum_{\l}\r_{\l}(t)|\l\bz\ket$, where
L000250	$|\Q_{g}\ket$ is the ground state and
L000251	$|\l\blQ\ket=\sum_{cv\blk}A^{\l\blQ}_{cv\blk}\hat{d}^{\dag}_{c\blk+\blQ}\hat{d}_{v\blk}|\Q_{g}\ket$
L000252	are the exciton states of momentum $\blQ$ -- here
L000253	$\hat{d}_{\m\blk}$ is the annihilation operator for electrons in band
L000254	$\m$ with momentum $\blk$. As the pump pulse
L000255	can only excite bright excitons,  $|\Q(t)\ket$ contains
L000256	exclusively excitons of vanishing momentum, $\blQ=\bz$. The coefficients
L000257	$\r_{\l}(t)=\sum_{cv\blk}A^{\l\bz\ast}_{cv\blk}\,
L000258	\bra\Q(t)|\hat{d}^{\dag}_{v\blk}\hat{d}_{c\blk}|\Q(t)\ket$ are the
L000259	exciton polarizations, and their square modulus yield the number of
L000260	coherent excitons, see Eq.~(\ref{N=c+ixb}). The
L000261	system is described by the state $|\Q(t)\ket$
L000262	up to times smaller than the exciton lifetimes.
L000263	Such time window defines the coherent regime. From
L000264	the knowledge of $|\Q(t)\ket$ we can directly calculate $G^{<}$, see
L000265	Appendix~\ref{lehmannapp}, and hence the
L000266	TR-ARPES spectrum. We refer to this strategy as the {\em Lehmann
L000267	approach}, since it is based on expanding the many-body state in
L000268	eigenstates of the Hamiltonian.
L000269	The same $G^{<}$ can be
L000270	obtained from Eq.~(\ref{G<}) using
L000271	the HSEX self-energy, see Eq.~(\ref{G<tmatfinld}).
L000272	The explicit form
L000273	of the HSEX self-energy can be readily derived
L000274	by projecting the equations of motion for the Green's
L000275	function~\cite{perfetto_pump-driven_2019,perfetto_time-resolved_2020} onto
L000276	the conduction-band subspace. The final result is
L000277	Eqs.~(\ref{sigma}) with $\s$ evaluated in
L000278	$N_{\l\blQ}=\d_{\blQ\bz}|\r_{\l}|^{2}$, see
L000279	Appendices~\ref{hsextwobandapp} and~\ref{hsexmultbandapp} for details.
L000280	The advantage of the many-body formulation over the
L000281	Lehmann approach is
L000282	that it successfully extends beyond the domain of low excitation
L000283	densities~\cite{pareek_driving_2026}.
L000284	
L000285	{\em Incoherent regime.--}
L000286	In the incoherent regime the
L000287	polarization $\r_{\l}$ vanishes, and consequently the HSEX
L000288	self-energy in Eqs.~(\ref{sigma}) vanishes too.
L000289	In this regime, the
L000290	electronic subsystem is described by an ensemble of bright and dark
L000291	incoherent excitons.
L000292	The transition from a pure state to an ensemble is a general
L000293	phenomenon in systems interacting with a bath, such as
L000294	electrons interacting with phonons in our case.
L000295	It has been demonstrated in an exactly  solvable two-band
L000296	model~\cite{stefanucci_from-carriers_2021,zhang_long-lived_2025},
L000297	and it is also a consequence of the excitonic Bloch
L000298	equations~\cite{thranhardt_quantum_2000,selig_exciton_2016,brem_exciton_2018,stefanucci_excitonic_2025}.
L000299	
L000300	A heuristic theory for the photocurrent in the incoherent regime
L000301	can be effectively developed for low excitation densities.
L000302	According to the excitonic Bloch equations the incoherent ensemble is described
L000303	by the many-body density matrix $\hat{\r}=|\Q_{g}\ket\bra\Q_{g}|+\sum_{\l\blQ}N^{\rm
L000304	inc}_{\l\blQ}|\l\blQ\ket\bra\l\blQ|$. From the knowledge of
L000305	$\hat{\r}$ we can calculate $G^{<}$, see Appendix~\ref{lehmannapp},
L000306	which in turn allows us to determine
L000307	the TR-ARPES spectrum. This is the Lehmann approach of the incoherent
L000308	regime~\cite{perfetto_first-principles_2016,sangalli_an-ab-initio_2018,rustagi_photoemission_2018,stefanucci_from-carriers_2021,chen_first-principles_2022}.
L000309	Establishing the many-body diagrammatic approximation
L000310	underlying this approach
L000311	would lift the low-density constraint, and pave the way toward
L000312	a fully first-principles treatment of TR-ARPES spectra in the
L000313	incoherent  regime.
L000314	
L000315	At present, the state-of-the-art many-body
L000316	approximation is largely based on
L000317	the T-matrix diagrams~\cite{kremp_equation_1984,semkat_ionization_2009,perfetto_first-principles_2016,steinhoff_exciton_2017}.
L000318	Previous studies reported
L000319	excitonic sidebands appearing as replicas
L000320	of the conduction bands~\cite{perfetto_first-principles_2016,steinhoff_exciton_2017},
L000321	in apparent contradiction to the Lehmann
L000322	approach, which instead predicts replicas of the valence bands.
L000323	Another issue pertains to the intensity of the photoemission signal,
L000324	proportional to $|A^{\l\blQ}_{cv\blk}|^{2}$. The
L000325	exciton wavefunctions satisfy the Bethe
L000326	Salpeter equation (BSE), whose
L000327	kernel is the sum of the bare
L000328	Coulomb interaction $v$ (direct term) and the screened interaction $W$
L000329	(exchange term)~\cite{onida_electronic_2002,strinati_application_1988,svl-book_2025}, i.e.,
L000330	\begin{align}
L000331	(\e^{\rm eq}_{c\blk+\blQ}-\e^{\rm eq}_{v\blk})A^{\l\blQ}_{cv\blk}-
L000332	\sum_{c'v'\blk'}
L000333	K^{\blQ}_{cv\blk,c'v'\blk'}A^{\l\blQ}_{c'v'\blk'}=
L000334	E^{\rm eq}_{\l\blQ}A^{\l\blQ}_{cv\blk}\;,
L000335	\label{eigeneqX}
L000336	\end{align}
L000337	with
L000338	\begin{align}
L000339	K^{\blQ}_{cv\blk,c'v'\blk'}=
L000340	W_{c\blk+\blQ\,v'\blk'\,v\blk\,c'\blk'+\blQ}-
L000341	v_{c\blk+\blQ\,v'\blk'\,c'\blk'+\blQ\,v\blk}.
L000342	\label{hsex}
L000343	\end{align}
L000344	Thus, a pure T-matrix self-energy (containing only
L000345	$W$) cannot yield the
L000346	Lehmann intensity of the signal.
L000347	
L000348	To reconcile many-body theory with the  Lehmann approach we consider the four self-energy
L000349	diagrams of Fig.~\ref{Tmatself}  -- the gray
L000350	circle is the exchange-correlation (xc) function $L$, the wiggly line
L000351	is the bare interaction $v$, and the double wiggly line is the
L000352	statically screened interaction $W$.
L000353	The first diagram in Fig.~\ref{Tmatself} is the T-matrix self-energy,
L000354	and  we refer to the sum of all four diagrams as the T-matrix plus
L000355	exchange (TX) self-energy.
L000356	Notice that the zeroth order xc function is simply $GG$. Consequently,
L000357	the lowest-order T-matrix diagram
L000358	has the same topology as the (second-Born) bubble diagram,
L000359	except that {\em both} interaction lines are screened.
L000360	This raises the issue of a possible double counting of screening
L000361	diagrams, which we address below.
L000362	
L000363	
L000364	The diagrammatic equation of Fig.~\ref{Tmatself} is
L000365	an approximation for the {\em lesser} and {\em greater} self-energy,
L000366	not for the time (or contour) ordered $\S$. Accordingly,
L000367	the bubble diagram with two $W$ lines does not emerge from T-matrix,
L000368	rather from GW. Indeed,
L000369	$\S_{\rm GW}^{<}=iG^{<}W^{<}=iG^{<}W^{R}P^{<}W^{A}$ where
L000370	$P^{<}=iG^{<}G^{>}$~\cite{svl-book_2025}.
L000371	Evaluating the screened interaction in
L000372	the static approximation, $W^{R}=W^{A}=W$, we recover
L000373	the lowest order (first)
L000374	diagram in Fig.~\ref{Tmatself}. Thus, there is no double counting
L000375	issue. We also observe that
L000376	the first diagram does not include
L000377	the {\em full} GW self-energy, since the bottom Green's function
L000378	is summed over
L000379	conduction bands only.
L000380	The missing contributions are recovered by adding the
L000381	fourth diagram in Fig.~\ref{Tmatself}. In fact, this diagram has the
L000382	structure $Gv\chi v=G(W-v)$, $\chi$ being the density response
L000383	function, and
L000384	$G$ is summed over the valence bands. In summary,  the
L000385	lesser and greater self-energies of Fig.~\ref{Tmatself} incorporate the full GW self-energy,
L000386	but handle $W$ differently depending on the Green's function band indices.
L000387	If $G$ has conduction indices then
L000388	$W$ is statically screened, whereas for valence indices $W$ is
L000389	dynamically screened.

L000496	&\times 2\p\d(\e^{\rm eq}_{v\blk-\blQ}+E^{\rm eq}_{\l\blQ}-\e+\w_{0}).

L000500	Refs.~\cite{perfetto_first-principles_2016,rustagi_photoemission_2018}
L000501	to multiple bands, and corrects the ansatz in
L000502	Ref.~\cite{chen_first-principles_2022} by placing the sum over
L000503	conduction bands inside the square modulus.

L000505	replica of the valence bands shifted in energy by $E^{\rm eq}_{\l\blQ}$
L000506	and in momentum by $\blQ$, see Fig.~\ref{spectrafig}(c).
L000507	It is worth observing that if the lowest-energy exciton, say $\l_{0}$,
L000508	is bright, and if we pump resonantly with it, then
L000509	$\r_{\l}(\t)\propto \d_{\l\l_{0}}$ (resonance condition).
L000510	As phonons do not scatter the exciton into higher energy states, the
L000511	coherent $\l_{0}$-exciton can only transition into an incoherent
L000512	$\l_{0}$-exciton of vanishing momentum. Considering the conservation of the total number of
L000513	excitons~\cite{stefanucci_excitonic_2025}, we infer that
L000514	$N_{\l\blQ}(\t)\propto \d_{\l\l_{0}}\d_{\blQ\bz}$ is  independent of $\t$.

L000516	in the coherent and incoherent
L000517	regimes~\cite{notepolaronic}.
L000518	Revealing the coherence of the system with TR-ARPES
L000519	requires a
L000520	probe field with a duration comparable to the exciton
L000521	period~\cite{perfetto_time-resolved_2020}.

L000538	The formula Eq.~(\ref{G<}) for $G^{<}$  simplifies if the wavefunction
L000539	of the occupied exciton states
L000540	have a predominant contribution on a single conduction
L000541	band and valence band, say $c_{0}$ and $v_{0}$. In this case,
L000542	$K^{\l\blQ}_{cv\blk}=\d_{cc_{0}}\d_{vv_{0}}K^{\l\blQ}_{c_{0}v_{0}\blk}$,
L000543	and the quantity $\s$ in Eq.~(\ref{sigmasmall}) has one single
L000544	nonvanishing entry for $c=c'=c_{0}$. This implies that also the
L000545	self-energy is nonvanishing only for $c=c'=c_{0}$. Defining
L000546	$\D_{\blk}^{\l\blQ}(\t)\equiv

L000548	depence of the various quantities on $\t$, we have
L000549	\begin{align}
L000550	G^{R}_{c_{0}c_{0}\blk}(\w)=\frac{1}{\w-\e_{c_{0}\blk}-

L000553	\label{twoband}
L000554	\end{align}

L000556	only a discrete number of excitons $\l_{j}\blQ_{j}$ are populated,
L000557	and that $ \D_{\blk}^{j}\equiv \D_{\blk}^{\l_{j}\blQ_{j}}$ are nonvanishing in small and
L000558	nonoverlapping regions $\callR^{j}$
L000559	of the first Brillouin zone. Then, for  $\blk\in \callR^{j}$ only
L000560	$\l_{j}\blQ_{j}$ contributes to the sum in the denominator of
L000561	Eq.~(\ref{twoband}). This allows us to calculate
L000562	$G^{<}_{c_{0}c_{0}\blk}$ analytically, see Appendix~\ref{hsextwobandapp} for details, and
L000563	find
L000564	\begin{align}
L000565	G^{<}_{c_{0}c_{0}\blk}(\w)\simeq 2\p i  \sum_{j}
L000566	\frac{E_{\l_{j}\blQ_{j}}+\e_{v_{0}\blk-\blQ_{j}}-E_{\blk,j}^{-}}
L000567	{E_{\blk,j}^{+}-E_{\blk,j}^{-}}\d(\w-E_{\blk,j}^{-}),
L000568	\label{G<i2}
L000569	\end{align}
L000570	where
L000571	\begin{align}
L000572	E_{\blk,j}^{\pm}&=\frac{1}{2}
L000573	\Big[\e_{c_{0}\blk}+E_{\l_{j}\blQ_{j}}+\e_{v_{0}\blk-\blQ_{j}}
L000574	\nn\\
L000575	&\pm\sqrt{(\e_{c_{0}\blk}-E_{\l_{j}\blQ_{j}}
L000576	-\e_{v_{0}\blk-\blQ_{j}})^{2}+4|\D_{\blk}^{j}|^{2}}\Big].

L000582	(low density limit) we can approximate the argument of the

L000610	{\em TR-ARPES in WSe$_{2}$ monolayer.--} We consider a WSe$_{2}$
L000611	monolayer (ML) at low ($n_{c}\sim 10^{11}$~cm$^{-2}$) and moderate
L000612	($n_{c}\sim 10^{13}$~cm$^{-2}$) excitation densities $n_{c}=N_{c}/A$,

L000616	estimated to be $\sim 2$~eV~\cite{lin_narrow-band_2021}.

L000618	Bose distribution
L000619	$N_{\l\blQ}=[e^{(E_{\l\blQ}-\m_{X})/T}-1]^{-1}$, where $T$ is the

L000623	exciton band structure, and how excitons are distributed
L000624	at temperature $T=70$~K; numerical details are reported in

L000627	excitons~\cite{deilmann_finite-momentum_2019,madeo_directly_2020},

L000631	at $K$ and $K'$ are populated. Along the path $\G-K-\G$, and
L000632	for low values of $n_{c}$, the spectrum features a single sideband

L000635	at the inequivalent $K$ point, which is the same as

L000666	
L000667	{\em Conclusions.--} We presented a first-principles approach to
L000668	excitons in TR-ARPES, bridging the coherent and incoherent regimes
L000669	through a unified formula that depends solely on the total number of
L000670	excitons at the pump-probe delay $\t$.
L000671	Applicable across a wide
L000672	range of temperatures and
L000673	excitation densities, our formula provides a powerful
L000674	tool for understanding and engineering nonequilibrium band structures
L000675	of excitonic materials.
L000676	Band hybridization with dark excitons enables
L000677	controlled shifts of the valence bands in both energy and momentum,
L000678	and to reshape them into a mexican-hat dispersion.
L000679	In particular,
L000680	the mechanism of
L000681	Ref.~\cite{foster_quench-induced_2014,perfetto_floquet_2020}
L000682	naturally extends to  the incoherent regime, enabling
L000683	control over the topological character of excited materials
L000684	through exciton wavefunction symmetries.
L000685	This points to a
L000686	promising avenue for realizing nonequilibrium
L000687	topological phases with
L000688	lifetimes reaching the picosecond timescale.

L000705	\section{Finite excitation-density corrections}

L000708	We here describe a practical method to estimate the finite-density
L000709	corrections to the quasi-particle and exciton energies from the sole
L000710	knowledge of the exciton populations $N_{\l\blQ}$.
L000711	
L000712	Let $\r_{\m\m'\blk}(t)=-iG_{\m\m'\blk}^{<}(t,t)$ be the one-electron
L000713	density matrix at time $t$. We define
L000714	$\r^{\rm eq}_{\m\m'\blk}=\d_{\m\m'}f^{\rm eq}_{\m\blk}$ as the
L000715	equilibrium one-electron  density matrix, with equilibrium occupations $f^{\rm
L000716	eq}_{v\blk}=1$ and $f^{\rm eq}_{c\blk}=0$. The change of the density
L000717	matrix  caused by an external pump pulse is then
L000718	\begin{align}
L000719	\D\r_{\m\m'\blk}(t)=\r_{\m\m'\blk}(t)-\r^{\rm eq}_{\m\m'\blk}.
L000720	\end{align}
L000721	This change induces the following change in the HSEX potential
L000722	\begin{subequations}
L000723	\begin{align}
L000724	V_{cc'\blk}(t)&=\sum_{vv'\blk'}\big(

L000750	energies can be estimated as
L000751	\begin{align}
L000752	\e_{\m\blk}=\e^{\rm eq}_{\m\blk}+V_{\m\m\blk},
L000753	\label{rqpene}
L000754	\end{align}
L000755	where
L000756	\begin{subequations}
L000757	\begin{align}
L000758	V_{cc\blk}&\simeq \sum_{v'\blk'}\big(
L000759	v_{c\blk\, v'\blk'\, v'\blk' \,c\blk}-W_{c\blk\, v'\blk'\,  c\blk\, v'\blk'}
L000760	\big)(f_{v'\blk'}-1)+\sum_{c'\blk'}\big(
L000761	v_{c\blk\, c'\blk'\, c'\blk' \,c\blk}-W_{c\blk\, c'\blk'\,
L000762	c\blk\, c'\blk'}
L000763	\big)f_{c'\blk'},
L000764	\label{epscR}
L000765	\\
L000766	V_{vv\blk}&\simeq \sum_{c'\blk'}\big(
L000767	v_{v\blk\, c'\blk'\, c'\blk'\, v\blk}-W_{v\blk\, c'\blk'\,  v\blk\, c'\blk'}
L000768	\big)f_{c'\blk'}
L000769	+\sum_{v'\blk'}\big(
L000770	v_{v\blk\, v'\blk'\, v'\blk'\, v\blk}-W_{v\blk\, v'\blk'\,
L000771	v\blk\, v'\blk'}\big)(f_{v'\blk'}-1).
L000772	\label{epsvR}
L000773	\end{align}
L000774	\label{epscvR}
L000775	\end{subequations}
L000776	In Eqs.~(\ref{epscvR}), the off-diagonal contributions of the density
L000777	matrix are discarded, i.e.,
L000778	$\D\r_{cc'\blk}\simeq \d_{cc'}f_{c\blk}$ and
L000779	$\D \r_{vv'\blk}\simeq \d_{vv'}(f_{v\blk}-1)$.
L000780	This is consistent with ignoring
L000781	finite-density corrections to the
L000782	quasiparticle wavefunctions. Thus, Eq.~(\ref{epscvR}) provides a
L000783	formula for the renormalized quasi-particle
L000784	energies in terms of the nonequilibrium occupations $f_{\m\blk}$.
L000785	
L000786	Let us now come to the renormalization of the exciton energies.
L000787	At finite excitation density, the BSE for the
L000788	exciton energies and wavefunctions reads
L000789	\begin{align}
L000790	\sum_{c'v'\blk'}H^{\blQ}_{cv\blk,c'v'\blk'}
L000791	\frac{A^{\l\blQ}_{c'v'\blk'}}
L000792	{\sqrt{f_{v'\blk'}-f_{c'\blk'+\blQ}}}=
L000793	E_{\l\blQ}\frac{A^{\l\blQ}_{cv\blk}}{\sqrt{f_{v\blk}-f_{c\blk+\blQ}}},
L000794	\label{bse1}
L000795	\end{align}
L000796	with
L000797	\begin{align}
L000798	H^{\blQ}_{cv\blk,c'v'\blk'}&=\d_{cv\blk,c'v'\blk'}
L000799	(\e_{c\blk+\blQ}-\e_{v\blk})
L000800	-\sqrt{f_{v\blk}-f_{c\blk+\blQ}}\,K^{\blQ}_{cv\blk,c'v'\blk'}
L000801	\sqrt{f_{v'\blk'}-f_{c'\blk'+\blQ}}
L000802	\label{bse2}
L000803	\end{align}
L000804	the BSE Hamiltonian.
L000805	We rewrite Eq.~(\ref{bse2}) as
L000806	\begin{align}
L000807	H^{\blQ}_{cv\blk,c'v'\blk'}=H^{{\rm eq},\blQ}_{cv\blk,c'v'\blk'}+\D
L000808	H^{\blQ}_{cv\blk,c'v'\blk'},
L000809	\end{align}
L000810	where $H^{{\rm eq},\blQ}$ is the equilibrium BSE Hamiltonian,
L000811	calculated with equilibrium occupations $f^{\rm eq}_{v\blk}=1$ and
L000812	$f^{\rm eq}_{c\blk}=0$, and
L000813	equilibrium band structure $\e_{\m\blk}=\e^{\rm eq}_{\m\blk}$.
L000814	To lowest order in $\D H^{\blQ}$ we have
L000815	\begin{align}
L000816	E_{\l\blQ}=E^{\rm eq}_{\l\blQ}+\sum_{cv\blk}\sum_{c'v'\blk'}
L000817	A^{\l\blQ\ast}_{cv\blk}\D
L000818	H^{\blQ}_{cv\blk,c'v'\blk'}A^{\l\blQ}_{c'v'\blk'},
L000819	\label{rxene}
L000820	\end{align}
L000821	where $E^{\rm eq}_{\l\blQ}$ is the equilibrium exciton energy and
L000822	$A^{\l\blQ}_{cv\blk}$ is the unperturbed exciton wavefunction.
L000823	
L000824	We express $\D H^{\blQ}$ in terms of the nonequilibrium occupations
L000825	$f_{\m\blk}$.
L000826	For the Pauli blocking factors we have
L000827	\begin{align}
L000828	\sqrt{f_{v\blk}-f_{c\blk+\blQ}}
L000829	\simeq
L000830	1+\frac{1}{2}\big(f_{v\blk}-f_{c\blk+\blQ}-1\big).
L000831	\end{align}
L000832	We conclude that to lowest order in the excitation density
L000833	\begin{align}
L000834	\D H^{\blQ}_{cv\blk,c'v'\blk'}&=
L000835	\d_{cv\blk,c'v'\blk'}\Big[V_{cc\blk+\blQ}-V_{vv\blk}\Big]
L000836	-\frac{1}{2}\big(f_{v\blk}-f_{c\blk+\blQ}+
L000837	f_{v\blk'}-f_{c\blk'+\blQ}-2\big)
L000838	K^{\blQ}_{cv\blk,c'v'\blk'},
L000839	\label{deltabse}
L000840	\end{align}
L000841	where $V_{\m\m\blk}$ is given in Eq.~(\ref{epscvR}).
L000842	
L000843	Equations~(\ref{rqpene}) and (\ref{rxene}) provide an approximation for the
L000844	nonequilibrium quasi-particle energies and exciton energies in terms
L000845	of the
L000846	nonequilibrium occupations. To  express these occupations in terms of exciton
L000847	populations we observe that for small excitation densities
L000848	the contribution of the $\l\blQ$-exciton to  $f_{c\blk}$ is
L000849	\begin{align}
L000850	\bra\l\blQ|\hat{d}^{\dag}_{c\blk}
L000851	\hat{d}_{c\blk}|\l\blQ\ket
L000852	&=\sum_{c_{1}v_{1}\blk_{1}}\sum_{c_{2}v_{2}\blk_{2}}
L000853	A^{\l\blQ\ast}_{c_{1}v_{1}\blk_{1}}
L000854	A^{\l\blQ}_{c_{2}v_{2}\blk_{2}}
L000855	\bra\Q_{g}|\hat{d}^{\dag}_{v_{1}\blk_{1}}

L000860	\end{align}
L000861	Therefore
L000862	\begin{align}
L000863	f_{c\blk}=\sum_{\l\blQ
L000864	v}N_{\l\blQ}|A^{\l\blQ}_{cv\blk-\blQ}|^{2},
L000865	\label{fck}

L000867	and similarly
L000868	\begin{align}
L000869	f_{v\blk}=1-\sum_{\l\blQ
L000870	c}N_{\l\blQ}|A^{\l\blQ}_{cv\blk}|^{2}.
L000871	\label{fvk}
L000872	\end{align}
L000873	Notice that the normalization of the exciton wavefunctions
L000874	guarantees that
L000875	$\sum_{c\blk}f_{c\blk}=\sum_{\l\blQ}N_{\l\blQ}$.

L000897	\section{Lehmann approach}
L000898	\label{lehmannapp}
L000899	The state of the system just {\em after} pumping ($t>0$)
L000900	can be written as
L000901	\begin{align}
L000902	|\Q(t)\ket=|\Q_{g}\ket+\sum_{\l}\b_{\l}e^{-iE^{\rm eq}_{\l\bz}t}|\l\bz\ket.
L000903	\label{cohstate}
L000904	\end{align}
L000905	The coefficients $\b_{\l}$ are proportional to the excitonic
L000906	polarizations since
L000907	\begin{align}
L000908	\r_{\l}(t)&=
L000909	\sum_{cv\blk}A^{\l\bz\ast}_{cv\blk}\,
L000910	\bra\Q(t)|\hat{d}^{\dag}_{v\blk}\hat{d}_{c\blk}|\Q(t)\ket
L000911	=\sum_{cv\blk}A^{\l\bz\ast}_{cv\blk}\,
L000912	\sum_{\l'}\b_{\l'}A^{\l'\bz}_{cv\blk}e^{-iE^{\rm eq}_{\l'\bz}t}
L000913	=\b_{\l}e^{-iE^{\rm eq}_{\l\bz}t}.
L000914	\label{rldef}
L000915	\end{align}
L000916	Thus, Eq.~(\ref{cohstate}) can also be written as
L000917	\begin{align}
L000918	|\Q(t)\ket=|\Q_{g}\ket+\sum_{\l}\r_{\l}(t)|\l\bz\ket.
L000919	\label{cohstate2}
L000920	\end{align}
L000921	For a pure state the Green's function is given by
L000922	\begin{align}
L000923	G^{<}_{\m\m'\blk}(t,t')\equiv i\bra\Q(t')|\hat{d}^{\dag}_{\m'\blk}e^{i\hat{H}(t-t')}
L000924	\hat{d}_{\m\blk}|\Q(t)\ket,
L000925	\label{g<def}
L000926	\end{align}
L000927	where $\hat{H}$ is the many-body Hamiltonian of the unperturbed system.
L000928	We have
L000929	\begin{align}
L000930	\hat{d}_{c'\blk}|\Q(t)\ket=
L000931	\sum_{\l}\b_{\l} e^{-iE^{\rm eq}_{\l\bz}t}\sum_{v}
L000932	A^{\l\bz}_{c'v\blk}\hat{d}_{v\blk}|\Q_{g}\ket.
L000933	\end{align}
L000934	Taking into account that $\hat{H}\hat{d}_{v\blk}|\Q_{g}\ket
L000935	=-\e^{\rm eq}_{v\blk}\hat{d}_{v\blk}|\Q_{g}\ket$,
L000936	we find for the Green's function in Eq.~(\ref{g<def})
L000937	\begin{align}
L000938	G^{<}_{cc'\blk}(t,t')=i\sum_{\l\l'v}\b_{\l}^{\ast}\b_{\l'}\;
L000939	A^{\l\bz\ast}_{c'v\blk}A^{\l'\bz}_{cv\blk}\;
L000940	e^{iE^{\rm eq}_{\l\bz}t'}e^{-iE^{\rm eq}_{\l'\bz}t}
L000941	e^{-i\e^{\rm eq}_{v\blk}(t-t')}.
L000942	\label{gfcohleh}
L000943	\end{align}
L000944	This Green's function depends on $t$ and $t'$ separately, due to the
L000945	interference of different exciton
L000946	states~\cite{rustagi_coherent_2019,zhang_long-lived_2025}. The Fourier
L000947	transform with respect to $t-t'$ is dominated by the diagonal
L000948	contributions and reads
L000949	\begin{align}
L000950	G^{<}_{cc'\blk}(\w)=2\p i\sum_{\l v}|\r_{\l}|^{2}\;
L000951	A^{\l\bz\ast}_{c'v\blk}A^{\l\bz}_{cv\blk}\;
L000952	\d(\w-E^{\rm eq}_{\l\bz}-\e^{\rm eq}_{v\blk}).
L000953	\label{gfcohlehw}
L000954	\end{align}
L000955	
L000956	For low excitation densities, the coherence between $|\Q_{g}\ket$ and the exciton states
L000957	$|\l\bz\ket$ is suppressed by electron-phonon scatterings on a
L000958	timescale that varies from a few tens to a few hundreds of
L000959	femtoseconds (depending on temperature and excitation
L000960	densities)~\cite{moody_intrinsic_2015,selig_exciton_2016,jakubczyk_impact_2018}. In the incoherent regime the
L000961	polarization $\r_{\l}$ vanishes, and the
L000962	electronic subsystem is described by an ensemble of bright and dark
L000963	incoherent excitons. From the many-body density matrix of the ensemble
L000964	$\hat{\r}=|\Q_{g}\ket\bra\Q_{g}|+\sum_{\l\blQ}N^{\rm
L000965	inc}_{\l\blQ}|\l\blQ\ket\bra\l\blQ|$, with $N^{\rm inc}_{\l\blQ}$
L000966	the number of incoherent excitons,  we can calculate
L000967	the Green's function  according to
L000968	\begin{align}
L000969	G^{<}_{cc'\blk}(t,t')=i\Tr\big[\hat{\r}\,e^{i\hat{H}t'}\hat{d}^{\dag}_{\m'\blk}e^{i\hat{H}(t-t')}
L000970	\hat{d}_{\m\blk}e^{-i\hat{H}t}\big]=
L000971	\sum_{\l\blQ}N^{\rm
L000972	inc}_{\l\blQ}G^{\l\blQ<}_{cc'\blk}(t,t'),
L000973	\label{g<ens}
L000974	\end{align}
L000975	where
L000976	\begin{align}
L000977	G^{\l\blQ<}_{cc'\blk}(t,t')&=i\bra\l\blQ(t')|
L000978	\hat{d}^{\dag}_{c'\blk}e^{i\hat{H}(t-t')}\hat{d}_{c\blk}|\l\blQ(t)\ket
L000979	\nn\\
L000980	&=ie^{-iE^{\rm eq}_{\l\blQ}(t-t')}
L000981	\bra\l\blQ|\hat{d}^{\dag}_{c'\blk}e^{i\hat{H}(t-t')}\hat{d}_{c\blk}|\l\blQ\ket
L000982	\nn\\
L000983	&=ie^{-iE^{\rm eq}_{\l\blQ}(t-t')}\sum_{v}
L000984	A^{\l\blQ\ast}_{c'v\blk-\blQ}A^{\l\blQ}_{cv\blk-\blQ}
L000985	e^{-i\e^{\rm eq}_{v\blk-\blQ}(t-t')}.
L000986	\label{G<isht}
L000987	\end{align}
L000988	In the incoherent regime the Green's function depends exclusively on
L000989	the time difference, and its Fourier transform reads
L000990	\begin{align}
L000991	G^{<}_{cc'\blk}(\w)=2\p i\sum_{\l\blQ v}N^{\rm inc}_{\l\blQ}
L000992	A^{\l\blQ\ast}_{c'v\blk-\blQ}A^{\l\blQ}_{cv\blk-\blQ}\;
L000993	\d(\w-E^{\rm eq}_{\l\blQ}-\e^{\rm eq}_{v\blk-\blQ}).
L000994	\label{G<ishtw}
L000995	\end{align}
L000996	Notice that if the population of incoherent excitons is given by
L000997	$N^{\rm inc}_{\l\blQ}=\d_{\blQ,\bz}|\r_{\l}|^{2}$, then the Green's
L000998	function -- and, consequently, the TR-ARPES spectrum -- becomes
L000999	identical for both the coherent and incoherent regimes.
L001000	This can be verified by comparing Eq.~(\ref{G<ishtw}) with the expression for the
L001001	Green's function in the coherent regime,
L001002	i.e., Eq.~(\ref{gfcohlehw}). Equations~(\ref{gfcohlehw})
L001003	and~(\ref{G<ishtw}), derived from the Lehmann approach,
L001004	agree with the Green's function in the many-body diagrammatic
L001005	approximation HSEX+TX, see Eq.~(\ref{G<tmatfinld}) in the main text.

L001007	\section{HSEX self-energy for two bands}
L001008	\label{hsextwobandapp}
L001009	
L001010	We consider a system with only one active conduction and valence
L001011	bands. The HSEX lesser and greater Green's functions for
L001012	resonant (not necessarily weak) pumping with the $\l$
L001013	exciton have been derived in Ref.~\cite{perfetto_pump-driven_2019}, and
L001014	for sufficiently low temperatures they have a simple analytic form
L001015	\begin{subequations}
L001016	\begin{align}
L001017	G^{<}_{cc\blk}(\w)&=2\p i
L001018	\frac{E_{\l\bz}+\e_{v\blk}-E^{-}_{\blk}}
L001019	{E^{+}_{\blk}-E^{-}_{\blk}}
L001020	\d(\w-E^{-}_{\blk}),
L001021	\label{G<ccprm}
L001022	\\
L001023	G^{>}_{cc\blk}(\w)&=2\p i \frac{E_{\l\bz}+\e_{v\blk}-E^{+}_{\blk}}
L001024	{E^{+}_{\blk}-E^{-}_{\blk}}
L001025	\d(\w-E^{+}_{\blk}),
L001026	\label{G>ccprm}
L001027	\end{align}
L001028	\label{Gccprm}
L001029	\end{subequations}
L001030	where
L001031	\begin{subequations}
L001032	\begin{align}
L001033	E^{\pm}_{\blk}&\equiv \frac{1}{2}\Big[
L001034	\e_{c\blk}+E_{\l\bz}+\e_{v\blk}
L001035	\pm S_{\blk}\Big],
L001036	\label{Eplusminus}
L001037	\\
L001038	S_{\blk}&\equiv\sqrt{(\e_{c\blk}-E_{\l\bz}-\e_{v\blk})^{2}
L001039	+4|\D_{\blk}|^{2}},
L001040	\\
L001041	\D_{\blk}&\equiv K^{\l\bz}_{cv\blk}\r_{\l}.
L001042	\end{align}
L001043	\end{subequations}
L001044	Setting $z=\w+i\eta$, the retarded Green's function is then given by
L001045	\begin{align}
L001046	G^{R}_{cc\blk}(\w)&=i\int\frac{d\w'}{2\p}
L001047	\frac{G^{>}_{cc\blk}(\w')-G^{<}_{cc\blk}(\w')}{z-\w'}
L001048	=\frac{z-E_{\l\bz}-\e_{v\blk}}{
L001049	(z-E^{+}_{\blk})(z-E^{-}_{\blk})}
L001050	=\frac{1}{z-\e_{c\blk}-\frac{|\D_{\blk}|^{2}}{z-E_{\l\bz}-\e_{v\blk}}},
L001051	\label{GRanalyt2}
L001052	\end{align}
L001053	from which we can read the retarded HSEX self-energy
L001054	\begin{align}
L001055	\S^{R}_{cc\blk}(\w)=\frac{|\D_{\blk}|^{2}}{z-E_{\l\bz}-\e_{v\blk}}-i\eta.
L001056	\label{twobself}
L001057	\end{align}
L001058	
L001059	To obtain the lesser HSEX self-energy we observe that
L001060	the Green's function in Eq.~(\ref{G<ccprm}) can also be
L001061	written as
L001062	\begin{align}
L001063	G^{<}_{cc\blk}(\w)=G^{R}_{cc\blk}(\w)\S^{<}_{cc\blk}(\w)G^{A}_{cc\blk}(\w).
L001064	\label{G<ccguess}
L001065	\end{align}
L001066	Let us show that this relation is satisfied for
L001067	\begin{align}
L001068	\S^{<}_{cc\blk}(\w)=-f(\w-E_{\l\bz}-\e_{v\blk})
L001069	\big[\S^{R}_{cc\blk}(\w)-\S^{A}_{cc\blk}(\w)\big],
L001070	\label{twobself2}
L001071	\end{align}
L001072	with $f(\w)=1/[e^{\w/T}+1]$ the Fermi function.
L001073	We have
L001074	\begin{align}
L001075	G^{R}_{cc\blk}(\w)\big[\S^{R}_{cc\blk}(\w)-\S^{A}_{cc\blk}(\w)\big]
L001076	G^{A}_{cc\blk}(\w)=G^{R}_{cc\blk}(\w)-G^{A}_{cc\blk}(\w)=
L001077	G^{>}_{cc\blk}(\w)-G^{<}_{cc\blk}(\w).
L001078	\end{align}
L001079	Therefore
L001080	\begin{align}
L001081	G^{R}_{cc\blk}(\w)\S^{<}_{cc\blk}(\w)G^{A}_{cc\blk}(\w)=
L001082	-2\p i f(\w-E_{\l\bz}-\e_{v\blk})
L001083	\Big[\frac{E_{\l\bz}+\e_{v\blk}-E^{+}_{\blk}}
L001084	{E^{+}_{\blk}-E^{-}_{\blk}}
L001085	\d(\w-E^{+}_{\blk})-\frac{E_{\l\bz}+\e_{v\blk}-E^{-}_{\blk}}
L001086	{E^{+}_{\blk}-E^{-}_{\blk}}
L001087	\d(\w-E^{-}_{\blk})\Big].
L001088	\label{gccguess2}
L001089	\end{align}
L001090	Next we observe that Eq.~(\ref{Eplusminus}) implies
L001091	\begin{align}
L001092	E^{\pm}_{\blk}-E_{\l\bz}-\e_{v\blk}&=
L001093	\frac{1}{2}\Big[
L001094	\e_{c\blk}+E_{\l\bz}+\e_{v\blk}
L001095	\pm S_{\blk}\Big]-E_{\l\bz}-\e_{v\blk}
L001096	\nn\\
L001097	&=\frac{1}{2}\Big[
L001098	\e_{c\blk}-E_{\l\bz}-\e_{v\blk}
L001099	\pm \sqrt{(\e_{c\blk}-E_{\l\bz}-\e_{v\blk})^{2}
L001100	+4\D_{\blk}^{2}}\Big]\gtrless 0
L001101	\end{align}
L001102	We conclude the second term in Eq.~(\ref{gccguess2}) dominates, and
L001103	we recover the analytic result in Eq.~(\ref{G<ccprm}).

L001105	\section{HSEX self-energy for multiple bands}
L001106	\label{hsexmultbandapp}
L001107	
L001108	In the general case, the Green's function in the HSEX approximation
L001109	can be obtained from the
L001110	equation of motion on the Keldysh contour~\cite{svl-book_2025}
L001111	\begin{align}
L001112	\Big[i\frac{d}{dz}-\e^{\rm eq}_{\m\blk}\Big]G_{\m\m'\blk}(z,z')
L001113	-\sum_{\n}V_{\m\n\blk}(t)G_{\n\m'\blk}(z,z')=\d(z,z'),
L001114	\label{eomGRmatk}
L001115	\end{align}
L001116	where the HSEX potential is given in Eqs.~(\ref{hsexpot}).
L001117	We look for an approximate solution of Eq.~(\ref{eomGRmatk}) in
L001118	the conduction subspace, which is the subspace we are interested in.
L001119	We discard
L001120	all matrix elements $V_{cc'}$ with $c\neq c'$
L001121	and $V_{vv'}$ with $v\neq v'$. This is equivalent to discard
L001122	finite-density corrections to the
L001123	quasiparticle wavefunctions. Although these corrections do not pose a conceptual
L001124	problem, they considerably complicate the practical implementation of
L001125	the theory. From Eq.~(\ref{eomGRmatk}) we  have
L001126	\begin{subequations}
L001127	\begin{align}

L001302	\section{Numerical details}
L001303	\label{numapp}
L001304	The electronic structure is described using a spin-resolved density functional theory (DFT) band dispersion
L001305	$\varepsilon_{n\mathbf{k}}$, mapped onto a tight-binding representation as detailed in Ref.~\cite{PhysRevB.88.085433}.
L001306	To match the experimentally measured quasiparticle band gap of about
L001307	$2.0~\mathrm{eV}$, a rigid scissor correction of
L001308	$0.5~\mathrm{eV}$ is applied to the conduction-band states $\varepsilon_{c\mathbf{k}}$
L001309	\cite{PhysRevLett.113.076802,Hsu_2019}.
L001310	The eigenstates of the Bloch Hamiltonian, denoted by $\mathbf{U}_{\mathbf{k}}$,
L001311	serve as the basis for constructing the Coulomb matrix elements that appear in both the
L001312	Bethe–Salpeter equation (BSE) kernel and the Hartree–screened-exchange (HSEX) Hamiltonian,
L001313	following the methodology of Ref.~\cite{perfetto_real-time_2023}.
L001314	
L001315	The Coulomb interaction is modeled using the Rytova–Keldysh potential
L001316	\cite{keldysh,PhysRevB.84.085406}, assuming a dielectric constant $\varepsilon = 1$
L001317	and a screening length of
L001318	$r_0 = 45~\mathring{\rm A}$ \cite{stier_magnetooptics_2018}.
L001319	To treat the divergence of the Coulomb potential $v_{\mathbf{q}}$ near the $\Gamma$ point,
L001320	we adopt the regularization scheme introduced in Refs.~\cite{PhysRevB.88.245309,PhysRevB.97.205409},
L001321	which consists of averaging $v_{\mathbf{q}}$ over a small region $\Omega$ around $\mathbf{q}=0$.
L001322	The size of this region is determined by the spacing of the Brillouin-zone sampling grid.
L001323	
L001324	In typical semiconductors, Coulomb matrix elements that involve processes changing the number of electrons
L001325	in the valence or conduction bands are vanishingly small and are therefore neglected
L001326	\cite{PhysRevB.93.205145}.
L001327	Since the Rytova–Keldysh interaction tensor $V$ in Eq.~(5) already incorporates
L001328	\emph{ab initio} static screening over the momentum scales relevant for excitonic physics,
L001329	the screened exchange interaction $W$ entering both the BSE kernel and the HSEX Hamiltonian
L001330	is approximated by $W \approx V$.
L001331	This simplification has been demonstrated to reproduce experimental exciton binding energies
L001332	with high accuracy in two-dimensional systems
L001333	\cite{steinhoff2,PhysRevLett.113.076802,PhysRevB.88.045318}.
L001334	
L001335	In the calculations presented here, the electronic subspace is limited to the two uppermost valence bands
L001336	and the two lowest conduction bands.
L001337	The Brillouin zone is sampled using a uniform mesh comprising $3072$ $\mathbf{k}$ points.
